T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based approach to design a responsive and user-friendly interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on accessibility and intuitive navigation.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems, including endpoints for creating, updating, deleting, and retrieving problems.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a schema to store problem details such as title, description, difficulty, tags, and test cases.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Build a code editor using a library like Monaco Editor or CodeMirror, with syntax highlighting and auto-completion features.
T4.notes: Ensure support for multiple programming languages.

T5.implementation_approach: Create an API to handle code submissions, including endpoints for submitting code and retrieving results.

T6.implementation_approach: Develop a system to execute submitted code in a secure sandbox environment and compare outputs with expected results.
T6.notes: Ensure security and prevent malicious code execution.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard interface to display user rankings, scores, and achievements.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user performance.
T8.notes: Optimize for real-time updates if needed.

T9.implementation_approach: Create a user profile interface to display user details, activity history, and achievements.
T9.notes: Ensure a clean and customizable layout.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profiles, including endpoints for retrieving and updating user information.

T11.implementation_approach: Connect frontend components with backend APIs using HTTP requests and state management libraries.
T11.notes: Ensure seamless communication and error handling.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the problem library.
T12.notes: Test edge cases and user interactions.

T13.implementation_approach: Test the code submission system by simulating various scenarios, including valid and invalid submissions.
T13.notes: Ensure the sandbox environment handles edge cases securely.

T14.implementation_approach: Test the leaderboard functionality, including data accuracy and sorting/filtering features.

T15.implementation_approach: Test user profile features, including data retrieval, updates, and UI responsiveness.

T16.implementation_approach: Deploy the application using a cloud platform, set up CI/CD pipelines, and configure environment variables.
T16.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor performance post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

# Function to access the database instance
def get_db():
    return db

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem(id={self.id}, title={self.title}, difficulty={self.difficulty})>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(50), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    # Define columns
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    # Set relationships
    user = db.relationship('User', back_populates='solutions')
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', back_populates='solutions')

# app/routes.py
# Layer: assembly
# Purpose: Aggregate all blueprints

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

# List of all blueprints to be registered
blueprints = [
    problem_blueprint,
    user_blueprint,
    solution_blueprint
]

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    # Create Flask app instance
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Configure database
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

    return app

from app import create_app

# Initialize the Flask application
app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A web application designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with support for multiple programming languages and real-time syntax highlighting.
- Submission System: A system to allow users to submit their solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- Leaderboard: A leaderboard to track user performance and encourage competition among participants.
- User Profiles: Personalized user profiles to track progress, achievements, and submitted solutions.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
